purpose: Translate vLLM engine requests into OpenInfer scheduler work and translate scheduler token events back into vLLM engine outputs.

actors.name: vLLM frontend
actors.role: Creates engine requests and receives engine output batches.

actors.name: bridge
actors.role: Translates request and response protocols inside bridge.rs.

actors.name: OpenInfer scheduler
actors.role: Accepts generation work and emits scheduled token events.

types.name: EngineCoreRequest
types.meaning: One request submitted by the vLLM frontend.

types.name: GenerateRequest
types.meaning: The scheduler request assembled by the bridge.

types.name: TokenEvent
types.meaning: A token or terminal event emitted by the scheduler.

types.name: EngineCoreOutputs
types.meaning: The output batch returned to the vLLM frontend.

coreFlows.name: Frontend request submission
coreFlows.why: The two engines use different request protocols and need an explicit translation boundary.

steps.why: The bridge must receive and recognize the Add request before translation.
The scheduler only accepts its own generation request contract.

coreFlows.name: Scheduler token return
coreFlows.why: Scheduler events must be folded into the frontend output protocol.

steps.why: The bridge is the consumer that batches each scheduler event.
The frontend requires token and finish information in its own output batch.

coreFlows.name: Immediate terminal output
coreFlows.why: Rejected requests still need a terminal response without entering the scheduler.

steps.why: The terminal helper reports directly to the frontend output channel.

supportingCapabilities.name: IPC readiness
supportingCapabilities.why: The bridge waits until the local endpoint exists before connecting.

supportingCapabilities.name: Scheduler statistics
supportingCapabilities.why: Frontend gauges need scheduler load snapshots independently of request output.

supportingCapabilities.name: Request tracing
supportingCapabilities.why: A request trace connects bridge submission with scheduler timing.

supportingCapabilities.name: LoRA selection
supportingCapabilities.why: Optional adapter selection is derived before scheduler submission.

supportingCapabilities.name: Utility responses
supportingCapabilities.why: Control calls return a frontend-compatible utility result.

supportingCapabilities.name: Stream cleanup
supportingCapabilities.why: Aborted or completed requests must release their bridge state.

functionRoles.why: Only Add requests should enter the normal generation path.
The scheduler needs its own request type and associated execution metadata.
Ready scheduler events must be reduced and sent as frontend output.
Token and terminal variants require different output fields.
Invalid requests must terminate visibly without scheduler submission.
Connection attempts must wait for the local endpoint.
Operational gauges are separate from request token output.
Scheduler spans need a request-level parent context.
Adapter configuration accompanies generation but is not the core transport path.
Utility calls bypass normal token generation.
Finished or aborted requests must not retain bridge state.

walkthrough.title: req-a Add request to token and Finished output

steps.text: The vLLM frontend sends req-a as an Add EngineCoreRequest and handle_message routes it to start_request.
start_request translates req-a into GenerateRequest and submits it to the OpenInfer scheduler.
The OpenInfer scheduler returns req-a TokenEvent values to dispatch_burst.
reduce_request folds req-a Token and Finished variants into EngineCoreOutputs.
dispatch_burst sends the resulting req-a EngineCoreOutputs to the vLLM frontend.

invariants.text: send_terminal_output sends EngineCoreOutputs to FrontendSender and never to the OpenInfer scheduler.
The normal response chain passes TokenEvent through dispatch_burst and reduce_request before frontend output.
